about: The living 'What we've found so far' panel at the top of the home page. Update after every batch or result: at most 7 items, most important first, plain numbers, each with a link. Bulletins (findings/bulletins/) are dated announcements; this file is the current state.

items.head: 35 of 40 famous megaliths are dated only by association.
items.text: Only Nan Madol has a direct date on its stones; the ages of the Great Sphinx, Carnac, Sacsayhuamán and others rest on nearby material, texts or style. We rank the 10 where a first direct date would matter most.

items.head: The Great Sphinx enclosure has never been dated directly.
items.text: A paired chlorine-36 test against Khafre-era quarry faces could show an older age, or confirm the accepted one.

items.head: Monte Verde, the textbook vindication, was reopened in 2026.
items.text: The challenger's own radiocarbon dates match the older age, and the key layer was destroyed decades ago.

items.head: Vindications are messy; refutations are clean.
items.text: Of 10 celebrated vindications, 3 held cleanly, 5 were partly right and 2 are still open. All 7 refutations held.

items.head: “It can't be that old” objections fail more often.
items.text: 25% of objections that proved wrong vs 8% of those that held: the predicted direction, not yet significant (p = 0.18). Four other hypotheses need more resolved cases.

items.head: Two database scans found nothing new.
items.text: No clustering among 173,946 radiocarbon dates. The 10 early-Americas candidates were contamination, miscoded samples or database errors; 4 remain unexplained only because their site reports were never published.
